history.period: Traditionally ancient; sources claim 1000 to 3000 years old - CONFLICT (verify)
history.summary: A major Bhadrakali shrine atop a hill, famous for its wall paintings, stone carvings and Kerala-style gopuram. Legend: two Namboothiris returning from Kollur Mookambika received an oracle that their Bhadrakali idol had her perpetual presence, and the goddess herself named Malayalappuzha as the site for it. The 5.5-ft, eight-armed idol is made of Katu Sarkara Yogam (concentrated jaggery with herbs/clay), showing the goddess in her fierce post-Darika form. It is the only Kerala temple where Satha Kodi Archana is performed (per webindia123 - verify). Devotees seek the goddess (also Idathattil Bhagwathi) for marriage, jobs, business and protection from enemies; Tuesday and Friday are the most auspicious darshan days. Antiquity claims conflict (1000 vs 3000 years). Administered by the Travancore Devaswom Board. The CSV 'state' column wrongly holds 'Pathanamthitta' (the district); actual town is Malayalapuzha, state Kerala. Evening hours conflict: 5-8 PM (pilgrimaide) vs 5-8:30 PM (velpu) - verify.

name: Malayalapuzha Devi Temple
town_description: Malayalapuzha is a hill village in Pathanamthitta district, central Kerala, about 8 km from Pathanamthitta town and 5 km from Kumbazha junction. A pilgrim hub in the Achankovilar-Kallar foothills, it is dominated by the Devi temple and draws devotees from across religions seeking the Amma's blessings.

travel.road: ~8 km from Pathanamthitta town via Kumbazha Malayalapuzha Road; buses and taxis available
